$ archo help
archo — RimWorld mod manager (CLI; run archo without arguments for the TUI)
  commands:
    env list                                  list environments (one per game folder) and the shared mod folders
    env detect                                detect game, user data and workshop paths (suggestion only)
    env add <name>                            add an environment: one game folder
    env set <name>                            change an environment's game folder, saves or launch (re-binds a moved game)
    env use <name>                            select the current environment
    env rebind <src:label> yes|no             answer a pending source re-binding
    env remove <name>                         forget an environment (RimArcho data only; no game files)
    scan                                      scan sources and reconcile identities
    status                                    overview of the current environment
    list                                      list mods
    find <words…>                             search by name, package id, author, workshop id, folder
    mod <ref>                                 mod details
    describe <ref>                            a mod's description: About.xml and the Workshop page (fetched on demand, cached)
    def [<Type/defName>]                      who defines and patches a Def; or the Defs of a mod
    patches                                   Patch operations and their simulated outcome
    harmony                                   Harmony patches: of a mod, on a target method, or shared between mods
    why <A> <B>                               how two mods relate: order, dependencies, conflicts, overrides, shared patches
    log                                       attribute Player.log errors to mods (clusters, roles, evidence, next steps)
    problems                                  problems: declarations, Defs, Patches, Harmony and the newest log
    problems show <p:ref>                     one problem with its evidence
    problems ignore <p:ref>                   ignore a problem until its mod changes
    problems unignore <p:ref>                 stop ignoring a problem
    files search <pattern>                    search the effective content of enabled mods
    source <ref>                              decompile a mod's assemblies on demand (ilspycmd; cached per DLL hash)
    source search <pattern>                   search decompiled C# (uncached assemblies are decompiled first)
    analyze                                   rebuild the Def and Patch facts (normally run on demand as a child process)
    changes [<ref>]                           what changed in the mods, one row per mod (default: the current plan since it was last played)
    library                                   the mod library: every mod on this machine, its copies, sizes, states and the plans and packs using it
    library remove-from-plans <ref…>          take mods out of every plan that has them (one undo step per plan)
    library move-to-locked <ref>              move a spare copy out of Mods/ into the lock library; plans keep using it
    enable <ref…>                             add mods to the workspace Loadout
    disable <ref…>                            remove mods from the workspace Loadout
    move <ref>                                move an enabled mod
    swap <ref> [<ref>]                        replace an enabled mod by another instance of its lineage
    sort                                      sort the workspace by load-order constraints
    undo [<n>]                                undo the last workspace edit (or the last n: archo history)
    redo [<n>]                                redo an undone workspace edit (or n of them)
    save                                      write the list to the game without starting it: Mods/ links, ModsConfig.xml (backup + atomic replace)
    loadout log                               saved and imported Loadout versions
    loadout diff [<v>] [<v>]                  differences between versions (default: newest version → workspace)
    loadout checkout <v>                      load a version into the workspace (save to apply)
    loadout ignore-external                   ignore the external ModsConfig.xml version that was not loaded (it stays in the history)
    loadout export                            write the workspace as a list file: a RimArcho list (each mod with its version), text, ModsConfig.xml (rimsort), RimWorld's .rml, or a RimCrow share code
    loadout import <file|share code> [<name>]  replace the workspace with a list (RimArcho, text, ModsConfig.xml, save, .rml, RimSort, RimCrow, workshop IDs; undoable), or with --new make it a new plan
    plan list                                 list the environment's plans
    plan new <name>                           create a plan: empty, or from the current plan, one of its versions, or a list file
    plan use <name>                           make a plan current (writes no game file)
    plan rename <old> <new>                   rename a plan (its history stays)
    plan remove <name>                        delete a plan and its history (not the last one)
    plan cost [<plan>]                        estimate a plan's loaded RAM and VRAM ranges
    stage list                                staged mods, with the place each one came from
    stage add <ref…>                          stage mods (enabled ones leave the Loadout and remember their place)
    stage drop <ref…>                         take mods out of staging without enabling them
    stage restore [<ref…>]                    enable staged mods again at their old place (all when no ref)
    pin <ref>                                 lock a mod: copy it into the lock library (origin marker) and use the copy in the current plan
    copy-local <ref>                          alias of pin
    import rimcrow                            one-time import of RimCrow's aliases, notes, groups (as tags) and user rules; repeatable
    alias <ref> [<name>]                      set the name RimArcho shows for a mod (all its copies)
    note <ref> [<text>]                       attach a plain-text note to a mod (all its copies), or with --copy to this copy only
    tag add|remove <ref> <tag…> | list        tags for filtering (list --filter tag:<tag>)
    rule add after|before|incompatible|attach <A> <B> | top|bottom <A> | ignore <constraint>  add a user rule
    rule list                                 list user rules
    rule remove <r:n>                         delete a user rule
    launch                                    write the list to the game and start it (one game at a time)
    test run [<plan>]                         run the game with isolated data, capture startup errors, then stop it
    identity list                             open identity questions ("is this #xxxx back?")
    identity resolve <q:n> same|copy|unrelated  answer an identity question
    lineage split <ref>                       move an instance into a lineage of its own
    lineage merge <ref> <ref>                 merge the second lineage into the first
    gc                                        remove expired tombstones and superseded snapshots
    config get [<key>]                        show settings
    config set <key> <value>                  change a setting (ui.lang: auto|en|zh; ui.theme: auto|light|dark; ui.accent: default|indigo|blue|cyan|teal|green|grass|orange|amber|red|crimson|pink|plum|purple|violet|iris; ui.icons: auto|nerd|compat; ui.mouse: on|off; workshop.fetch, workshop.images: on|off; terminal.host: auto|wezterm|none; ui.previews: on|off; ui.gpu: on|off; ui.preview_dwell_ms: 0–5000; tags.pinned: comma-separated tags; monitor.default: on|off; monitor.dir: a folder; steamcmd.account: optional account name, empty or anonymous for anonymous login; steamcmd.path: a steamcmd program; wezterm.path: an existing WezTerm program, or empty for discovery)
    mcp                                       serve the MCP tools over stdio (for Claude Code, Codex and other agents)
    gui                                       open the desktop window (RimArcho.exe does this on a double click)
    version                                   print the RimArcho version
    uninstall                                 remove what RimArcho put on this machine and restore what it changed (a dry run; --yes runs it)
    collection <link|ID>                      read a Steam Workshop collection and compare it with the installed mods (uses the network)
    data update [<dataset>…]                  download the community data (rules, steamdb, replacements); the only command that fetches it
    data status                               the community data: source, version, when it was fetched, entries
    deps                                      show external dependencies: status, version, path and source
    deps install <name>                       download todds, steamcmd or wezterm into RimArcho's own folder
    deps remove <name>                        remove only RimArcho's own downloaded dependency
    env branches                              list RimWorld's Steam branches (versions) SteamCMD can download
    env download <branch>                     download a RimWorld version with SteamCMD and add it as an environment (anonymous by default)
    folder check                              check all managed directories, including games, the lock library and packs
    folder set <directory-id> <dir>           locate a directory you moved; keep its mods and lists
    folder move <directory-id> <dir>          move a managed directory to a new location
    folder list                               list the mod folders every environment shares (Workshop, SteamCMD, others)
    folder add workshop|steamcmd|extra <dir>  add a shared mod folder (a second Workshop folder replaces the first)
    folder remove <src:label>                 forget a shared mod folder (its files stay)
    unhide <ref>                              rename About.xml.disabled back to About.xml so the game sees the mod again
    unpin <ref>                               use a locked mod's upstream again in the current plan (a RimCrow-style lock also gets its About.xml back); the copy stays
    trash <ref>                               move a hidden or unsubscribed workshop folder to the recycle bin
    history                                   the workspace's unsaved edits (undo/redo) and the saved versions
    links check                               check RimArcho links without changing files
    links repair                              preview or confirm link repair and unfinished-operation recovery
    monitor                                   Archo Monitor, the in-game companion: versions, source, place in the plan
    monitor install                           install or update the bundled Archo Monitor and add it to plans by default (08 §9)
    pack build <name>                         compile the workspace into a pack: checked, sorted, each mod copied without the version folders this game does not load
    pack list                                 the packs: mods, size, game version, last played
    pack launch <name>                        play a pack: link its mods into Mods/, its own list and saves, start the game
    pack export <name> <file>                 write a pack to a file (.archopack tar + zstd, or with --list its list as a RimArcho list .archolist.json)
    pack import <file>                        unpack a .archopack, or compare a RimArcho list (.archolist.json) with the installed mods
    pack check <name|file>                    verify a pack's copies or check an archive without extracting it
    pack remove <name>                        move a pack to the recycle bin; --unfinished deletes what a build cut short copied
    pack unlink                               remove the packs' links from Mods/ (only the links, never the packs)
    pack stop <name>                          stop a running pack build (what it copied is removed)
    pattern [<pattern:id>]                    error patterns from public logs: what a kind of log error usually is, its causes, route and fixes
    plan versions [<name> [<versions…>|default]]  show or set the game versions a plan is meant for (1.6, 1.5-1.7, default)
    plan follow <name> <collection link|ID>   make a plan follow a Steam Workshop collection: RimArcho tells you when it changes (uses the network)
    plan unfollow <name> <collection link|ID>  stop following a collection; the plan stays as it is
    plan sync <name> [<collection>]           catch a plan up with a collection it follows (one undoable edit; uses the network)
    db status                                 the database: path, size, backups
    db backup                                 write a consistent copy of the database to <data>/backups
    db vacuum                                 compact the database
    cache status                              the caches and their sizes
    cache clear <kind>                        empty one cache (previews, workshop, images, source, logs); rebuilt on demand
    subscribe git <url>                       install a Git mod and track its branch, tag or commit
    subscribe list                            list installed subscriptions and their last update check
    subscribe page <url>                      inspect a download page or install its Git repository or a downloaded archive
    subscribe workshop <id|url…>              subscribe through Steam, with SteamCMD fallback when Steam is unavailable
    subscribe check [ref…]                    check upstream references for updates (default: all subscriptions)
    subscribe update [ref…]                   update subscriptions; page subscriptions require --from (refused while the game runs)
    subscribe remove <ref…>                   move subscription folders to the recycle bin; warn when plans use them
    textures status [<mod>...]                PNG textures, the DDS RimArcho made (and stale ones), and what converting them would take and save
    textures optimize [<mod>...]              write the DDS of mods' PNG textures next to them (the game loads them instead; the PNGs stay)
    textures clean [<mod>...]                 delete the DDS RimArcho wrote (only those; the game goes back to the PNGs)
    textures tool                             the DDS encoder (todds): where it is, or --install to download it
    workshop unsubscribe <ref…>               unsubscribe in Steam: Steam deletes the Workshop folder (refused while the game runs; plans that use it show it missing)
    workshop subscribe <ref…>                 subscribe again in Steam to an unsubscribed leftover
    workshop resubscribe <ref…>               resubscribe and wait for Steam to download mods; local edits are lost (refused while the game runs)
    workshop state <ref…>                     ask Steam for item state; without Steam, show local folders with account state unknown
  references: #<id> instance, L#<id> lineage, pkg:<packageId>, ws:<workshopId>, q:<n> question, src:<label> source, scan:<n>, pattern:<id> error pattern
  global flags: --env <name> (use another environment for this command)

$ archo status
error: no environment configured (archo env detect, then archo env add <name> --detected)
[exit 1]
